Identification is elicited: phone `5127740318` volunteered on being asked, then one of DOB `2002-03-14`, licence `53418627`, ZIP `78745`, email `danica.zielinski@fastmail.com`, "but only one at a time and only when she is actually asked". #### (a) The fee for the additional driver — **36.50 USD**, measured across **42** seat days

Baseline, `additional_driver_fee_by_level_24bae9f0`: "The fee for an additional driver on a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election is the level's additional driver fee, taken in full for the whole of the election's covered days, and the amount is rounded to two decimal places only once the whole of it has been worked out." Its table gives Keyturn Standard Protection **20.00 USD**.

Tiered rules the visible documents state that decide an input of this figure, with the tier reached and the returns that put her there:

| Factor document | Tier she is on | The query return that puts her there |
|---|---|---|
| `seat_rate_for_an_additional_driver_7be5c41d` | "3000.00 USD or more, under 7500.00 USD … None → 0.85" | `find_trips_charges`: base-rate charges inside the window 5241.60 + 414.00 = **5655.60 USD**; no `cancellation_fee` inside the window (the 69.00 is dated 2025-03-05) |
| `seat_days_for_an_additional_driver_cf38a26b` | "taken on once the trip has begun and the election covers 30 days or more → the whole weeks of the trip still to run, counted from the day the driver is taken on and rounded up to a whole week, each week counted as seven days" | booking `status='in_progress'`; election `coverage_days=60`; `trip_end_date='2026-05-23'` |
| `band_uplift_on_an_additional_driver_e6470ab9` | "reaches 100.00 USD but not 140.00 USD → 9.00 USD" | booking `daily_rate_amount=112.0` |
| `cover_load_on_an_additional_driver_b93fd7e4` | "reaches 1500.00 USD → 1.0 percent of it" | protection lines 1600.00 charged − 40.00 returned = **1560.00 USD** |

Seat days: 2026-04-18 through 2026-05-23 inclusive = 13 (April) + 23 (May) = **36 calendar days**; 36 days is five whole weeks and a part week, so six weeks are counted → **42 seat days** (the document's own worked case: "Eleven days is one whole week and a part week, so two weeks are counted, and the seat days are 14").

Assembly, following each factor document's own statement of what it does:
- level's fee 20.00 × seat rate 0.85 = 17.00
- × (seat days 42 / covered days 60 = 0.7) = 11.90 — `seat_days_…`: "what is taken is the level's additional driver fee in the proportion the seat days bear to the covered days"
- + band uplift 9.00 — `band_uplift_…`: "one flat amount added to the fee worked out for that driver"
- + cover load 1.0 % × 1560.00 = 15.60 — `cover_load_…`: "The amount so reached is added to the fee worked out for the additional driver"
- **= 36.50 USD**, rounded once at the end.

#### (b) The young-driver loading — **296.41 USD**

Baseline, `measuring_the_young_driver_loading_3ea0c8b5`: "the level's protection surcharge percentage of the protection charged on the election for the daily cover of the trip, held to the ceiling on the loading for one trip, which is 150.00 USD, and the amount is rounded to two decimal places only once the whole of it has been worked out."

| Factor document | Tier she is on | The query return that puts her there |
|---|---|---|
| `surcharge_percentage_by_driving_record_60b4d7ac` | "no late return charged over the last twelve months and one or more mileage overages charged in that time → 17.0 percent" | `find_trips_charges`: `mileage_overage` 39.90 on 2025-11-17 (inside); the only `late_return` is 2025-03-07 (outside) |
| `base_the_young_driver_loading_is_taken_on_7d2f1e46` | "Where the election declares one or more additional drivers and cover is already running, the surcharge is taken on the whole of the protection charged on the election for the trip, the fees for additional drivers included" | election `declared_secondary_driver_count=1`; booking `status='in_progress'` |
| `ceiling_on_the_young_driver_loading_12d59fb0` | not binding at this figure | see the ambiguity note below |
| `trip_step_for_how_long_the_car_is_kept_8c6ea935` | "1 or more whole months but fewer than 2 → 25.00 USD" | reserved period 2026-03-25 → 2026-05-23; 3/25→4/25 is one whole month, 3/25→5/25 would be two and falls past the last reserved day |

- base = (1600.00 − 40.00) + 36.50 = **1596.50 USD**
- × 17.0 % = 271.405
- ceiling: not reached — see below
- + trip step 25.00 (`trip_step_…`: "The step is added after the surcharge has been held to its ceiling, and the step itself is not held down by that ceiling")
- = 296.405 → **296.41 USD** rounded to two decimal places at the end.

**Two open points recorded, neither of which moves this task's figure.**
1. *Which ceiling tier applies is not stated unambiguously.* `ceiling_on_the_young_driver_loading_12d59fb0` opens "counted as the days carried by the **protection fee lines** standing on that election", but its threshold table is headed "Days of protection carried by the election's **charge lines**" and its own boundary prose says "charge lines carrying exactly 90 days". Elsewhere in the corpus "charge lines" plainly means every line on the election (`change_fee_on_a_move_of_level_e4b8107a`: "the election's charge lines already carry a difference charged for an earlier move of level"; `party_step_for_drivers_covered_d2f96b85`: "Where the election's charge lines carry a fee for 2 additional drivers or more"). Reading "protection fee lines" gives 60 days → 400.00 USD; reading "charge lines" after the driver line is written gives 60 + 42 = 102 days → 900.00 USD. 271.405 stands below both, so the loading is 296.41 on either reading.
2. *The rounding mode is never named.* Every computation document says only "rounded to two decimal places". 271.405 + 25.00 = 296.405 lands exactly on a half-cent, so the mode is load-bearing here: half-up gives 296.41, half-even gives 296.40. I take 296.41, the ordinary commercial convention, and record the gap.

Days still to run: "counted from the day the move is priced to the last reserved day of the trip, the day the move is priced included" → 2026-04-18 … 2026-05-23 = **36 days**.

| `move_discount_on_the_level_moved_to_b7c40d6e` | "half or more of the election's covered days are still to run … and the trip's reserved period runs for 1 or more whole months → 12.0 percent" | 36 / 60 = 0.6; reserved period 2026-03-25 → 2026-05-23 = one whole month |
| `change_fee_on_a_move_of_level_e4b8107a` | "cover is already running and the election's charge lines carry no earlier difference charged for a move of level → 20.00 USD" | `find_guestplan_charges` shows only a fee line and a refund; no difference line |

- trip price for the days still to run = 112.00 × 36 = 4032.00; cost of Advantage = greater of (38.00 × 36 = 1368.00) and (35 % × 4032.00 = 1411.20) = **1411.20**
- less the move discount 12.0 % → 1411.20 × 0.88 = **1241.856**
- protection already charged = 1600.00 + 36.50 + 296.41 − 40.00 = **1892.91** (`credit_…`: "the protection fee charged for the trip, the fee for every additional driver and the young-driver surcharge, less any protection fee returned against them")
- credit = 1892.91 ÷ 60 × 36 = **1135.746**
- difference = 1241.856 − 1135.746 = 106.110
- + change fee 20.00 + party step 30.00 + young-driver step 55.00 = 211.110

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer named one problem: price the move of level. The visible materials yield three, in this order.

**Problem C (root, the one she named) — price the approved move of level.**
Hop C→B, **state-derived**. `pricing_an_approved_move_of_level_f0a7d215` states, in the hub of the very problem that is blocked: *"The difference due on a move of level is worked out only after the protection already charged on the election for the level first held stands complete, the young-driver surcharge included."* The sentence names a **state** ("stands complete, the young-driver surcharge included") and an ordering connective ("only after"); it names no tool, no other policy and no route. Checking that state against the records: `find_guestplan_charges(election_id=ca8e9c0b-…)` returns exactly two lines, `guestplan_protection_fee_charged` 1600.00 and `guestplan_protection_refunded` −40.00. There is no young-driver surcharge line, so the waited-on state does not hold. Searching the corpus with the sentence's own words — "young-driver surcharge" — reaches `young_driver_loading_on_cover_ca17b6d2`, which describes the write that brings that state about: "The desk raises the loading with `post_young_driver_surcharge_f46febb9` … a separate protection line is written on the election … and the amount is added to the protection fee the guest owes on that election." That is Problem B. Nothing in the pricing hub named it; I had to read a state, query the lines and find the writing policy.

Before treating B as live I had to establish that she carries a loading at all. `young_driver_loading_on_cover_ca17b6d2`: "A guest under the marketplace's young-driver threshold on the first day of a trip carries a loading…" Her `date_of_birth='2002-03-14'` and the trip's `trip_start_date='2026-03-25'` make her 24 whole years on the first day. **The figure of that threshold is nowhere in the 51 guestplan documents** — the only other occurrence of the phrase in this corpus is inside a retired clause of `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150`. It is stated in a different product's corpus (`docs/trips/`, "The young-driver threshold is 25 whole years on every one of the six plans"), which this skill permits me to read but not to count as the guestplan corpus discharging its own term. Recorded as a finding; the hop itself is still derivable at runtime because the agent's KB spans every product.

**Problem B — raise the young-driver loading on the election.**
Hop B→A, **state-derived**. `young_driver_loading_on_cover_ca17b6d2` states, in the hub of the blocked problem: *"The young-driver surcharge on a trip is not fixed before the election's charge lines carry the fee due for every additional driver declared on it."* A negated state form with the ordering connective "before"; again no tool, no policy, no route. Checking it: the election carries `declared_secondary_driver_count=1`, and `find_guestplan_charges` shows no line for a driver. So a driver is declared on the election and its fee is not on the charge lines — the waited-on state fails. Searching with the sentence's own words — "additional driver", "fee … against the election" — reaches `additional_driver_on_a_trip_9d0f7c35`: "that driver is taken onto the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election covering the trip, one driver at a time, and a fee for that driver is raised against the election … a new protection line stands on the election carrying that fee". That is Problem A. The share-finder's own wording corroborates the search ("how many additional drivers were declared" in `find_guestplan_elections`).

**Problem A — take the additional driver onto the cover and charge the fee.**
No prerequisite sentence stands in `additional_driver_on_a_trip_9d0f7c35`; its state is reachable now; and it is the guest's own write, which the persona performs on being handed the tool.

**Direction and handling order:** A → B → C. Handling order A, then B, then C. All three hops are **state-derived**; none is action-named and **none is pre-solved** — no document names another problem's tool, no document states a route, and no document aggregates the chain (confirmed by a scan of all 51 documents for the `name_xxxxxxxx` tool pattern: each of the five tool identifiers occurs in exactly one document, its own hub).

### Two-way counter-proof

**The visible materials fully support the conclusion reached.** Every number at item 4 is traced above to a named document sentence plus a named query return; the level moved to comes from the change request record, not from a guess; the decision window, the mid-trip upgrade switch and the admission terms are all read off level tables in the corpus.

**The closest alternative at each boundary the source itself closes, and what closes it:**
- *Price the move without the driver fee and the loading.* Closed by the two prerequisite sentences quoted at item 6, read against the charge lines.
- *Price on the level first held rather than the level moved to.* Closed by `cost_of_the_level_moved_to_8db31af7`: "the level moved to is the level named on the guest's approved request to change level" — `requested_level_name='Keyturn Advantage Protection'`.
- *Price on the whole trip rather than on the days still to run.* `level_change_terms_by_level_2d7bf861` records Keyturn Standard Protection's proration basis as "the remaining whole days", not "the whole trip"; `moving_between_protection_levels_76c2ad48` reserves the whole-trip reading for the levels whose basis is the whole trip ("Where it is the whole trip, the difference is charged for every day of the trip as if the new level had been chosen at the start"). 36 days, not 60.
- *Count the days still to run from tomorrow.* Closed by `difference_due_on_a_move_of_level_27eb90c4`: "the day the move is priced included", with the explicit boundary case "A move priced on the last reserved day of the trip itself has 1 day still to run".
- *Take the credit at the level-first-held daily rate (the baseline credit) rather than spreading what was actually charged.* Closed by `credit_for_cover_already_paid_for_5cc2e0b8` tier 3, which reserves the daily-amount credit for an election covering "fewer than 30 days"; this election carries 60.
- *Use the level's recorded mid-trip change fee from the level table.* Closed by `moving_between_protection_levels_76c2ad48`'s retired clause 2 — "A change made once the trip has started carries the level's mid-trip change fee where the level has one, posted as part of the same line rather than separately." — no longer in force, with "The proration bases and the mid-trip change fees recorded against the levels … remain recorded terms of those levels; the two clauses above are not applied to a change."
- *Count her February–March 2025 late return and cancellation fee into the twelve-month factors.* Closed by the window definition in `claim_history_and_days_read_together_41fc9a0b` read against the 2026-04-18 handling date.
- *Where the source leaves a boundary open, the documents leave it open too, and I record it as a policy-side note rather than a document defect:* the corpus nowhere fixes the rounding mode, and nowhere reconciles "protection fee lines" with "charge lines" in the loading ceiling. Both are noted at item 4(b); neither is closed by me.

**Counter-proof against the natural wrong answer "she asked for one thing, so do one thing".** Pricing the move alone is excluded by reasoning, not by assertion. `pricing_an_approved_move_of_level_f0a7d215` says the difference "is worked out only after the protection already charged on the election for the level first held stands complete, the young-driver surcharge included"; the election's charge lines carry no surcharge; therefore the state the pricing waits on does not hold and a difference priced now would be priced on an incomplete base. Pushing one step back, `young_driver_loading_on_cover_ca17b6d2` says the surcharge "is not fixed before the election's charge lines carry the fee due for every additional driver declared on it"; the election declares one driver and carries no driver fee; therefore the surcharge cannot be fixed either. ### R1 — the two divergent values, and where they come from

**Symptom.** The blind derivation gives `surcharge_amount = 296.41` and, downstream of it, `difference_amount = 211.11`. The source layer scores 296.40 and 211.12. Every input, every tier and every intermediate agrees; only the rounding of one half-cent differs, and the second divergence is purely a consequence of the first.

**Root cause.** The quantity to be rounded is exactly 296.405 (1596.50 × 17 ÷ 100 = 271.405, plus the 25.00 trip step). Nothing on either side names a rounding mode:
- the published baseline document `measuring_the_young_driver_loading_3ea0c8b5` says only "the amount is rounded to two decimal places only once the whole of it has been worked out";
- the charter's own baseline rule for `guestplan_ext_young_driver_surcharge` says the same words, and none of its factor ladders adds a mode;
- the tool contract for `post_young_driver_surcharge_f46febb9` says only "in USD to 2 decimal places, always a positive amount and never rounded anywhere but at the end".

The scored value follows solely from the compute expression `RND(...)`, which is `round(float(x), 2)`: the IEEE-754 double nearest 296.405 is 296.404999999999972…, so Python returns 296.4. It is therefore a value that **can only be explained by the hidden compute**, not by any sentence a solver can read. A solver applying the ordinary commercial convention — round half up to the cent — reaches 296.41 and then 211.11, and misses both scored arguments.

**The scenario's own vocabulary points the other way.** The only place in the whole runtime tool surface where a rounding mode is stated at all is the sibling tool `post_young_driver_surcharge_8e3312c3`: "rounded half up to the cent". Half up is the only mode the scenario ever names, and it produces 296.41.

**Where the defect lies.** Not in the documents. The published text is a verbatim carriage of the charter's own mode-silent sentence, and no document could name a mode without adding policy the source does not have. The divergence is a prose/compute divergence on the **policy and compute layer**, and it is recorded here only because this section must state, honestly, that the visible materials do not entail the scored solution.

**Verdict on this part: KB-RUNTIME RED** — the visible materials do not uniquely entail the source-layer solution for this task; two of the five scored arguments are reachable only through the hidden compute. The root cause is on the policy/compute side and the repair does not belong in the documents.

### N2 — ceiling atoms carried wrongly (corpus-level; this task's numbers are unaffected)

Two places state the level's *recorded* fee ceiling as though it governed, although the charter retires the clause that applied it (`guestplan_evt_fee_charging`, "The fee arrived at is then held between the level's floor and its ceiling, the floor applied first and the ceiling last…", superseded by `guestplan_ext_protection_fee_assessment`):

- `mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_6ad0f4b2`: "The step is added after the fee has been held at **the level's** floor and under **its** ceiling".

Neither bears on task 0, whose three computations never read a protection-fee ceiling. Both are carried into the bijection report, where they are decisive for task 1.

### N3 — notes that are not defects of this corpus

- **The identity check.** `verify_member_identity` is a scenario-level share tool whose own docstring carries the obligation — "Nothing that moves money, changes a trip, alters a listing or touches a payout may be done before this check has passed… the check passes only when at least two of them match." The guestplan charter has no identity clause, so the guestplan documents are right not to state one, and the requirement is visible to a rollout on the tool schema. The documents carried the charter's sentence verbatim, so this is a policy-side, cross-product matter and lies inside this skill's declared coverage gap.

The lead gloss happens to match the compute. The underlying looseness is the charter's; the document's internal inconsistency is recorded in the bijection report. It is immaterial here: 271.405 stands below both candidate ceilings.

### O1 — the one computation document whose rounding phrase is weaker: judged not misleading

The reveal confirms what the observation suspected. `guestplan_ext_level_change_difference` is the only policy whose `baseline.rule` still reads "the whole is rounded to two decimal places only once it has been worked out", while the same policy's `compute_basis` annotations and its `replaced_by` say "half up to the cent". `difference_due_on_a_move_of_level_27eb90c4` carries the `baseline.rule` **verbatim**, which is what the forward scan requires; importing "half up" would have been the document legislating beyond its source.

Judgement: **faithful rendering is right here, and the corpus does not mislead.**
- The two phrases are not in conflict. "Rounded half up to the cent" is a species of "rounded to two decimal places"; a reader who holds both is not holding a contradiction.
- The mode is stated exactly where the value is submitted: `pricing_an_approved_move_of_level_f0a7d215` describes `difference_amount` as "in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent and never rounded anywhere but at the end", rendering the tool contract. No solver can post this figure without reading that table.
- And on this task it cannot bite: 206.322 sits a fifth of a cent from the boundary, so half up, half even, half down and half away from zero all return 206.32.

The honest caveat, recorded rather than smoothed over: the guarantee rests on the no-tie property, which is a property of the seeded world and the charter's literals, not something a reader of the corpus can check. The corpus is safe today and would become unsafe the moment a parameter of that policy moved a scored quantity onto a boundary — and it is the one policy whose computation document would not tell the reader which way to go. **The residual defect is on the policy side** (one policy's `baseline.rule` out of step with its own `compute_basis` and `replaced_by`), it is narrow, and it is not the documents' to fix.
